target.title: fix(core): use UTF-16-safe truncation for chat display, ACP stream relay, and native hook relay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three truncation helpers in core used raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can split supplementary-plane characters (emoji, CJK extension B+, etc.) into lone surrogate halves when the cutoff lands between a high/low surrogate pair. This produces malformed UTF-16 in user-visible display text — the same class of bug as #99566, which fixed the exec approval command display path.

| Site | Cap | Risk |
|------|-----|------|
| `chat-display-projection.ts` — `truncateChatHistoryText` | 8 KiB | Very high — core display pipeline, every chat message goes through it |
| `acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` — `truncate()` | 220 chars | High — short boundary, agent streaming output often contains emoji |
| `native-hook-relay.ts` — `truncateText()` | 80/240/700 chars | Medium-high — approval UI, same surface as #99566 |

## Summary

- Switch all three truncation helpers to `truncateUtf16Safe` imported from `../utils.js` (re-exported from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`), matching the pattern used by other callers like `tool-display-exec.ts`, `tool-display-common.ts`, and `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`.
- Add regression tests: construct a string with an emoji whose surrogate pair crosses the truncation boundary, verify no lone surrogate in output.
- The fix is mechanical: each site changes one `value.slice(0, N)` call to `truncateUtf16Safe(value, N)` and adds one import.

## Evidence

### Real runtime proof (Linux, Node 24.13.1, commit dc114e4b)

All three runtime paths exercised via vitest (`--disable-console-intercept --reporter=verbose`) against the production modules with real emoji-at-boundary strings. Each path confirmed no lone surrogates in the truncated output:

```
# chat-display-projection: 25-char input ("a"×19 + "😀" + "tail") at 20-char boundary
[PROOF] truncateChatHistoryText: input=25 maxChars=20 safeLen=19 hasLoneSurrogate=false

# acp-spawn-parent-stream: 228-char input ("a"×218 + "😀" + "moretext") at 220-char boundary
[PROOF] acp truncate: input=228 maxChars=220 safeLen=218 hasLoneSurrogate=false

# native-hook-relay: 242-char input ("c"×236 + "😀" + "tail") at 240-char boundary
[PROOF] native-hook-relay truncateText: input=242 maxLength=240 safeLen=236 hasLoneSurrogate=false
```

- `safeLen` consistently backs off to avoid splitting the surrogate pair (19 instead of 20, 218 instead of 219, 236 instead of 237)
- `hasLoneSurrogate=false` in all cases — zero orphaned surrogates in output

### Focused tests
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts \
  src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts
```
→ 6 files, 124 tests passed (12 gateway + 112 agents)

### Import resolution
- `pnpm tsgo --project tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` on all 3 changed source files — clean
- All three files import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `../utils.js` (or `../../utils.js`), consistent with upstream/main's canonical re-export path

### Lint & Format
- `oxfmt --check` on all 6 changed files — clean

## Revision (2026-07-05)

Rebased on `upstream/main` (17a1993f13). Import paths fixed to target `../utils.js` instead of the removed `../shared/utf16-slice.js`. Stale tsconfig references to the old path removed (covered by `packages/normalization-core/src/**/*.ts`).

## Risk

Low. This only changes the truncation boundary to back off from split surrogate pairs. It does not change truncation caps, markers, redaction logic, or any product behavior.
